The other options in chat were "Fix the allow rule" (remove the deny entry, which needs their approval and a session restart) and "Re-cut #391 only" (ask again next time). The brief listed the third option as "the delivery lead merges". That was 11886 (c), not the option they were shown when they chose. No typed message followed the selection. (2) **The trigger case, read by master** (git after `git fetch --prune`, GitHub API). PR #391 (AQP-303, STORY-05.03, `feat/AQP-303-part-form`, head 3058848) has one commit, whose parent is 7d369e6. It is `mergeable` false and `dirty` against `master` d60415d. Its only CI run, 43609861840 (created 15:22:45Z, merge ref with ba059dd), failed in every job at type-check or build: `tests/integration/masters/customer-delete.test.ts(41,25)` TS2345: in the merged tree, the dependencies object that this test builds is not assignable to `EstimateDependencies`. #391 does not touch that file, which came with #388. So the re-cut has a **type clash outside its own files**, besides the text clashes. The files changed both by #391 and by `master` since 7d369e6 are 10, not the 2 that 11886 names: `estimate-texts.ts`, `route-manifest.ts`, `material-repository.ts`, `engineer-import-rule.test.ts`, `fake-masters.ts`, `route-calls.ts`, `route-loaders.ts`, `session-harness.ts`, `spec-access.ts` and `http-route-manifest.test.ts`. (3) **What the standing rule requires** (DL-212 (4), made general; the orchestrator puts it in every re-cut brief). (a) Branch `<old branch>-2` (or the next free suffix: `-3`, and so on) from `origin/master` after `git fetch`. Never reuse a name. (b) Re-apply the commits with `git cherry-pick`, or by hand in the editor if that is refused. Never use another command to get round a refusal, and never force-push. (c) Before resolving, list the clash set: `git diff --name-only <old branch's fork point> origin/master` intersected with the PR's files. Keep both sides in every clashing hunk. After that, run `tsc` (locally if memory allows, else in CI) and fix any type clash in files the PR does not touch, as in (2). Name in the PR body every hunk that is not a plain keep-both, and every such fix, with the reason. (d) Run the local Gitleaks scan over the new commits before the first push, with test IDs in named constants (DL-213). (e) Run targeted Vitest and ESLint locally. The merge gate is a fully green CI (§9 item 1). (f) For a `critical-review` story, the combined review (§9 item 2) reads the new head. An earlier review carries over only if it shows that the new diff equals the old one outside the resolved hunks and the named fixes. (g) The new PR body says "Supersedes #N". The old PR is closed unmerged, with a comment linking the new one. (h) The orchestrator records each re-cut as one line in the daily update and as an occurrence under RISK-030. A re-cut needs no new DL entry unless it departs from (a) to (g). (4) **Where it does not apply.** A PR that is only behind `master`, with no conflict, is updated with GitHub's "update branch", as #389 and #390 were. The rule covers only the denial of `git merge origin/master`. It authorises no settings change and no other command. It does not cover Dependabot PRs (CLAUDE.md §8). If the allow rule is later fixed, a developer merge becomes the first route again, and this rule becomes the fallback. (5) **Old branches.** Agents cannot delete branches. 11886 (a) said "you delete old branches in batches", but the option text they chose does not say that. Deleting the leftover branches (`feat/AQP-306-delete-guard`, `feat/AQP-296-own-work-status`, `feat/AQP-303-part-form` once re-cut, and any later ones) therefore stays on the delivery lead's batch clean-up list as housekeeping, as in DL-212 (5). The exception, as before: if a (3)(d) scan finds a flagged line, the old branch holds it too, and its deletion becomes an immediate DL-188 ask, because CI scans every branch. (6) **Cause still not established.** On `master` (unchanged since 68f6bf3), `.claude/settings.json` holds the allow `Bash(git merge origin/master)` (line 29) and the deny `Bash(git merge origin/master *)` (line 66). The orchestrator's view that the deny also matches the bare command is still a hypothesis, because the same settings let AQP-299's developer merge earlier on 2026-11-14 (DL-212 (2)). This decision supersedes DL-212's recommendation to put option (3) to the delivery lead again on a third re-cut. | **Why it is acceptable:** each re-cut keeps the agents inside their permissions, changes no history on `origin` and no setting, and once both sides are kept, it gives the tree a merge would give. CI and the critical review then read that tree. **Costs accepted by the delivery lead:** new SHAs and a new PR per case, a review re-read for `critical-review` stories, and leftover branches until their batch clean-up. **Alternatives not chosen:** fix the allow rule (a settings change and a restart, with the cause unproven); re-cut #391 only and ask again each time. **Master's note:** the #391 case shows that "keep both sides" is not enough on its own. This includes "Stages 1 to 11", 11b, the four E2E shards, the Windows package, "Capacity and latency (NFR-010, NFR-011)", the Lighthouse run and the warm-cache job. #593 (head 5b7b45e3, BEHIND): "CI feedback time" and "Sweep, keyboard flows and browsers (NFR-016, NFR-018, NFR-019)" red. Nightly run 44918456783 (event `pull_request`, #588's head), job 136889124766 log: "only 4 runs, fewer than the 20 asked for: p95 28 m 06 s, median 22 m 05 s"; the runs used were 44913181454 (head 34575e39) to 44916045921 (head 2e9655fe), and none of them is #588's. The step ended with exit code 1 after its threshold lines, not on a script error. **Trigger:** `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` on `origin/master` already has `pull_request` (branches `master`) with a `paths` filter that lists `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` itself (STORY-10.10 A-2, test strategy 10.2). The job `ci-time` has no `if:`. Read against the merge base, #588 adds 133 lines to nightly.yml (the `capacity` job and header) and #593 adds 153 (the `browsers` job, header and `paths` entries for its own files); neither changes the `on:` block or the `ci-time` job. **So neither PR adds the trigger:** the existing trigger fires because each PR edits nightly.yml, and every job then runs, `ci-time` included. `scripts/lib/ci-feedback-time.ts` on `origin/master` has no 13-run floor: it reports "fewer than 20" and still fails. That conflicts with test strategy 10.3 item 4 (fewer than 13 runs is "not a reading" and is used for no CI-time decision), and it is the open GitHub #328. The final review reports (`docs/06-reviews/final/`) do not grade CI time, so §9 item 3 is not triggered. (2) **Ruling (a).** §9 item 1 states its own test: a story PR merges "as soon as every required check is green", and it lists what is not loosened (lint, type-check, unit tests, E2E at three widths, the secret scan, the cost-confidentiality scan, branch protection). "CI feedback time" is none of these. It is not a required check, nightly.yml's header says "It never blocks a merge", test strategy 10.3 says "A breach never blocks a merge", and DL-235 (C) ruled that it "is not a required check and is not a merge criterion". It does not test the PR's head: it reads the durations of other runs, so its result does not depend on the PR's content. **"Fully green" therefore means:** every required check green, and every other check reported on the head green, except "CI feedback time" under these conditions: **C1** its failure is the threshold result of `check-ci-time.ts` (the p95, median or 9-minute lines, with any run count), not a crash, error, time-out or cancellation; **C2** the PR does not change `scripts/check-ci-time.ts`, `scripts/lib/ci-feedback-time.ts` or the `ci-time` job block of nightly.yml (a PR that does is the one place the measure is checked, and comes to master); **C3** every other Nightly job on the head is green, in particular a job the PR itself adds, which is story evidence ("Capacity and latency" for #588; "Sweep, keyboard flows and browsers" for #593, which is not excluded and must be green); **C4** strict up-to-date: after "Update branch", the run on the updated head is the run of record, and C1 to C3 are read again on it. **Applied:** #588 meets C1 to C3 on da9dde79 and merges once its updated head reads the same. #593 meets C1 and C2, and merges when its browsers job is green and its updated head reads the same. **Ends** at G8 sign-off, or earlier if the delivery lead makes the job a merge criterion. (3) **Ruling (b).** On a pull-request run the job measures nothing about that PR. Its red result only appears on PRs that edit the files listed in the `paths` filter, so it is noise in the merge decision. The fix is a tooling change, which §9 item 4 freezes, and master does not override the freeze (DL-235). **PG-CI-1 (post-G8, owner solution-architect, then developer):** (i) run `ci-time` only on `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch`, or on a pull request only when C2's files change; (ii) implement test strategy 10.3's window rule and the 13-run floor (#328), so a window under 13 runs reports "not a reading" and does not fail; (iii) then take the first valid reading (at least 13 runs) and re-score RISK-023 on it. The orchestrator records PG-CI-1 on #328 (a comment, or a linked follow-up issue). (4) **Ruling (c).** CI feedback time is a delivery-pipeline target (test strategy 10.3, written as PROPOSED). RISK-023 records it as agreed by the delivery lead. A breach slows feedback to the team; it does not put users, data, security or correctness at risk, and the final review raised no finding on it. **G8 treatment:** RISK-023 stays open at 8 and goes into the G8 risk-register review with these figures. They are the last valid reading, 14 runs, p95 22 m 23 s and median 16 m 17 s (DL-235), and the later windows under 13 runs (8 runs on 20 Nov, 4 runs on 21 Nov), which are not readings under test strategy 10.3 item 4. Master re-assesses impact there (the I 2 basis no longer holds, DL-235). It is not a G8 blocker. **G8-C-CI (owner: delivery lead, due G8):** at sign-off the delivery lead accepts in writing that the CI feedback-time target is not met at release, with PG-CI-1 as the plan after G8. Master's G8 recommendation lists it under known limitations of the delivery pipeline, not of the product. | Why (a): the words of §9 item 1, the job's own header, test strategy 10.3 and DL-235 all say that this job is not a merge condition. C1 to C4 keep the exclusion narrow: a broken measure, a change to the measure, or a red story job still holds the PR. Why (b): the freeze is the delivery lead's, and the noise costs one known red line per PR, not a risk. Why (c): the target is the delivery lead's, so a miss at release is theirs to accept knowingly.
